texts.preamble: Bharat Madan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 July, 2024 Author: Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia Bench: Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Jabalpur Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia On The 3rd Of July, 2024 Misc. Criminal Case No. 26536 of 2024 (Bharat Madan And Others Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others) Appearance: (By Shri Maneesh Kholia - Advocate) (By Shri Gajendra Parashar - Panel Lawyer) Order
texts.facts: 1. This application under section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed seeking the following reliefs :- "It is therefore prayed that this Honourable Court may kindly be pleased to quash the FIR No.966/2019 dated 22.9.2019 registered by police station Civil Lines District Rewa against the applicants and also to quash proceedings in Criminal Case No. RCT/137/2021 pending before Court of JMFC Rewa in the interest of justice". 2. It is submitted by counsel for the applicants that applicant No.1 is the husband, applicant No.2 is father-in-law, applicant No.3 is mother-in- law and applicant No.4 is younger brother-in-law of the respondent No.2. The respondent No.2 has lodged an FIR to the effect that she got married to the applicant No.1 on 7/12/2015 in accordance with Hindu rights and rituals. At that time, the applicant No.1 was working in a Company in Germany. The marriage was attended by the family members of both the families. Her father had given a cash of Rs.10 Lacs as well as had also borne the entire expenses of the marriage performed in Khajuraho. A gold chain, ring and a bracelet was given to her husband whereas gold ornaments were also given to applicants No.2 to 4. After her marriage, she went to her matrimonial house at Kanpur where she had stayed for a week. The applicants were demanding an amount of Rs.10 lacs and a car and also started harassing her on account of the same. Thereafter, she went to Germany and resided with her husband for about three months and during this period she was harassed physically and mentally by her husband on account of demand of dowry. The said conduct of the applicant No.1 was also informed by her to her parents. During her stay in Germany as well as in Kanpur the applicants were regularly demanding Rs.10 lacs and a four Bharat Madan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 3 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180559118/ 1 wheeler and on account of non- fulfillment of the said demand they were harassing the respondent No.2 physically and mentally. In the month of January 2019, she came to Rewa along with her husband to visit her parental house. Even in her parental home which is situated in Rewa the demand of dowry was made by the applicants. Since her parents could not fulfill their demand, therefore, she was left by her husband in Rewa. Thereafter, her parents tried to convince the applicants and accordingly, in the month of February, 2019, she went to Germany to reside with her husband but he brought her back to India in the month of April and from May, 2019, she is residing in her parental home. Her parents also went to Kanpur to pursue the applicants but they did not agree and demanded that unless and until an amount of Rs.10 lacs and a car is given, they would not allow the respondent No.2 to stay in her matrimonial house. Initially, she did not lodge a report but, thereafter, she approached the Parivar Paramarsh Kendra but the applicants did not agree for discussion. The gold and other articles given at the time of marriage are with the applicants and accordingly the FIR was lodged. 3. Challenging the FIR lodged by the respondent No.2, it is submitted by counsel for the applicants that applicants No.2 to 4 were not residing along with the applicant No.1 as well as respondent No.2, therefore, the allegations made against them are false. It is further submitted that initially respondent No.2 had also filed a petition for divorce which was ultimately withdrawn by the respondent no.2. She had also filed an application under section 125 Cr.P.C. which too was withdrawn by her and only after applicant No.1 filed a petition for divorce, the FIR in question was lodged by way of counter blast. It is further submitted that now a decree for divorce has been granted by judgment dated 29.2.2024 passed by the Principal Judge, Family Court, Rewa in RCSHM No.184/2023. 4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner. The FIR was lodged on 22.9.2019 whereas the applicant No.1 had filed the divorce petition on 24/7/2023.
texts.arguments: It is further submitted that it is well established to principle of law that for prosecuting the near and dear relatives of the husband of the complainant, the allegations should be clear, specific and direct and vague, omnibus and general allegations are not sufficient to compel the near and dear relatives of the husband to face the ordeals of the trial. 15. It is submitted by counsel for the applicant that on account of overall assessment of the allegations made against the applicants it is clear that the same have been made out of the malafide intention. The counsel appearing for the appellant also drew our attention to the same decision which is relied upon in the impugned judgment by the High Court i.e. State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal.
